t_psd.why: x87 excess precision in four1/realfft reaching Psd's decibels. Under -fexcess-precision=fast modern GCC keeps 80-bit intermediates the object narrows to 32 bits mid-butterfly, and by the time the transform reaches a decibel the divergence is up to 0.043 dB on bins near -85 dB, where cancellation dominates. It is NOT closable with a tolerance: the smallest separation between two V90PreFilter reference loops that give DIFFERENT answers is SSD 0.00268 dB^2 (AscendNULL vs AscendNULLCodec2, refLoopsType2), a distance of 0.0518 dB, and 0.043 dB on six points moves a signature by 0.105 dB -- four times the separation, so the excess precision can flip autoSelection's winner. `Psd::getFrequencies` is the same register one site over and is NOT the FFT: the object computes `(long double)i * sampleRate * (1.0L / m_length)` as three extended steps with one rounding at the store -- `fildll m_length`; `fld1`; `fdivrp`; `fildll i`; `fmul %st(2),%st`; `fmul %st(1),%st`; `fstps (%esi,%ecx,4)` at .text+0x469ed..0x46a0e -- while the modern `-ffast-math` profile reassociates it to a single multiply with a reciprocal (`fildll`; `fdivrs <sampleRate>`; `fildl`; `fmul`; `fstps`), 1 ULP on bin 39 (got 1139243841, reference 1139243840). `-fno-associative-math` restores a two-multiply form, but the object's own profile is `-ffast-math`, and the period compiler at those exact flags does NOT reassociate: period passes all 8169 getFrequencies checks. `make period` passes all of t_psd's groups: the period compiler has no divergence here, and it is the tier that decides.

checks: V90Equalizer: the shift at an exact power of two
t_v90equ.why: The same one-ordered-compare equality as t_agc, at six sites: `linearEquBeta != beta` and `dfeBeta != beta` in the two setters (`flds 0x10(%ebx); fcomp %st(1); fnstsw; sahf; je`, one compare, no parity test), `beta != 0.0f` in each setter's fixed-point arm, and `linearEquBeta != 0.0f` / `dfeBeta != 0.0f` in convertEqualizerToMmx (`fcom %st(1)` against `fldz` and `je`). The other four checks are consequential: enterPhase3, freeze, enterRRN/enterFPE and enterPhase4 all reach one of those six and they went green together on the period tier when the six were corrected. Finding F2300 for the sites, 2304 for why no modern flag closes it. `the shift at an exact power of two` is `convertEqualizerToMmx`'s fixed-point conversion run at beta values that are exact powers of two, and it is the x87 excess-precision half rather than the compare half: the object's four float accumulators are stored back to four-byte stack slots every iteration (`fstps 0x4c(%esp)`, `fstps 0x48(%esp)` at .text+0x374bb and +0x3750b, and the DFE pair at 0x37967/0x379ac), and the modern `-ffast-math` build keeps conversion intermediates in x87 and rounds differently, so the converted arrays at V90Equalizer+204/+208/+269/+272 differ in 80 of 105 checks. The period compiler at the same flags rounds at those stores: period passes all 105. `make period` passes this binary's twenty groups and 208,311 checks.

checks: V90Phase4Demodulator: the keep-rate flag on an unordered dB
t_v90p4dnan.why: `params->RRN_SILENCE_MIN_ECHO_ENERGY_FOR_KEEP_RATE < dB`, stored into +0x3510 at the tail of CalcErrorEnergyAfterEchoCancellation. The object issues ONE ordered compare and no parity test -- `flds 0x10(%esp); flds 0x404(%ebx); fcompp; fnstsw; sahf; setb %dl` at 0x26956..0x26976 and again at 0x275a0..0x275c6 -- so an UNORDERED result leaves CF set and the flag comes out 1. `dB` is unordered whenever the two silence energies have opposite signs, because then `1.0f / after * before` is negative and `fyl2x` answers a NaN. IEEE C requires a relational compare against a NaN to be false and GCC 13 emits the parity test whatever it is told, so the modern build stores 0 and cannot be made to store 1 from correct source; `-ffinite-math-only` is rejected on finding F2304's ground. THE OPERAND ORDER IS THE FIX AND NOT THE DECLARATION: written `dB > PARAM` the site is wrong under the object's own flag too, which is finding F2301's shape, and t_v90p4ddec's negative-accumulator trial is what caught it. IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose: an excused binary exits non-zero, and tools/mutate.py judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, so a red binary cannot score a mutation set and refuses. Splitting the check out is what that refusal asks for, and it leaves t_v90p4ddec's three sweeps -- 65,984 checks -- green under both compilers and mutation-testable. `make period` has no allow-list and passes all four groups with the object's own compiler.

t_v90equproc.why: x87 excess precision on `float err = soft - fdec` inside `V90Equalizer::process`. The object subtracts two values it has already narrowed to `float` in memory and leaves the DIFFERENCE in a register (`fsub %st(1),%st` at 0x394ef); that difference then feeds the squared-error accumulator, the DFE step and the high-error test, and GCC 3.4.2 spills it -- rounding it back to `float` -- only where a call forces the x87 stack out. Where `soft` is past a short's range the RESET slicer returns the x87 indefinite -32768, so the exact difference needs ONE bit more than a `float` carries and the spilled and unspilled readings part company; half an ulp there is hundreds of counts in `word_78`. The `the phase 4 state arms` group reaches the same subtraction from the phase-4 state path and fails 1 of 18023 for the same reason. THE SAME SOURCE IS EXACTLY GREEN ON THE PERIOD COMPILER: 120,974 differential checks, 0 failed, GCC 3.4.2 at the project's own flags, and period passes all 18023 of the phase 4 state arms. On GCC 13 it fails 731, and the failures are `word_78`, `word_7c`, `meanErrorEnergyCurrent` and the connection evaluator's average -- every one of them downstream of that one subtraction. IT IS NOT CLOSABLE BY CHOOSING A TYPE, and all three candidates were measured: `long double err` gives 59 on GCC 13 and is wrong on 3.4.2 as well; forcing the narrowing at every use (`volatile float` round trip) gives 733 on GCC 13 and 1 on 3.4.2; the plain `float` the author wrote gives 731 and 0. The object's own behaviour is not expressible portably -- it rounds at some uses and not others, and which is which is the register allocator's -- so the source is the object's, `make period` proves it, and the modern build declares. `-fexcess-precision=standard` would close it and is a translation-unit-wide change to flags this tree derived from the object; finding F1453's t_psd entry is the same class with the same disposition.

t_v90specproc.why: INHERITED, NOT NEW: `V90SpectralVerifier::process` calls `Psd::process` on the sample that completes an accumulation, and `Psd::process` already carries this register's t_psd entry -- finding F1453, x87 excess precision in four1/realfft reaching the decibel scaling, up to 0.043 dB and explicitly not closable with a tolerance. The divergence arrives in this binary as 1 and 2 ULP disagreements in the 32 spectrum bins the periodogram writes: 181 of 35,450 checks on GCC 13, every one of them a `spectrum bin` comparison and none of them a return value, a state, a counter, an accumulation buffer or a transcript. Nothing this binary tests about `process` ITSELF diverges. `make period` passes all four groups and every one of the 35,450 checks with the object's own compiler and the object's own flags, over the same inputs and not a subset -- so the source is right and the modern build is what cannot reproduce it, which is finding F1453's ruling one call deeper. IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose, for the reason t_v90p4dnan's entry gives: an excused binary exits non-zero, tools/mutate.py judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, and a red binary cannot score a mutation set. The other seven members of the class are in t_v90specacc.cpp, which is green under both compilers and is where their mutation set lives.

checks: V90ConnectionEvaluator: evaluatePhase4's replacement-threshold sign on an unordered PDSNR_CURRENT_V34_DROP_THRESH_PHASE4
t_v90connevalnan.why: `V90ConnectionEvaluator::evaluatePhase4` prints its replacement threshold `t` (`params->PDSNR_CURRENT_V34_DROP_THRESH_PHASE4`) through the object's branchless sign select at 0x3fdb7: `fldz`; `fcom %st(1)`; `fnstsw %ax`; `sahf`; `sbb %esi,%esi`; `and $0xfffffffe,%esi`; `add $0x2d,%esi` -- `0x2d - 2*CF`, ONE ordered compare and no parity test. FCOM sets CF for an UNORDERED `t` exactly as for `0.0f < t`, so the object prints '+' for a NaN. The source carries the object's spelling `!(0.0f >= t) ? '+' : '-'` (finding F2410), and `make period` reproduces the object: this binary's four checks and the t_v90conneval tag-7500 block are green on GCC 3.4.2 with the object's own flags. The modern build compiles `src/` with the recovered `-ffast-math` source profile (`CXXMATHFLAGS`), which implies `-ffinite-math-only`, so GCC 14 is entitled to assume no NaN and folds the ternary to `fstp %st(0); setbe %dl; lea 0x2b(%edx,%edx,1),%edx` -- `setbe` is CF or ZF, both set for an unordered compare, so the modern build prints '-' where the object prints '+'. The period compiler receives the same `-ffast-math` and does NOT perform the fold, which is why one compiler reproduces the object and the other cannot; there is no source spelling that serves both, because `(0.0f < t)` prints '-' on the object too. This is finding F2304's class one site further, and F4812's shape: modern GCC folds an ordered compare under an assumption the object's code does not make. IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose: an excused binary exits non-zero, `tools/mutate.py` judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, and a red binary cannot score a mutation set. Splitting the transcript check out of `t_v90conneval` is what that refusal asks for, and it leaves that file's 8,846 checks green under both compilers and mutation-testable (its 213-mutation `v90conneval` set). The set's row for this site is recorded `why_uncaught`, because the modern tier cannot separate the two spellings for a NaN; `make period` is where that claim lives. Issue #143.
